prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets from market data, which made it possible to measure market power and the effects of mergers and regulation

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed from B030 to B005. I apply one test to every candidate, and I chose it before looking at where colleagues stand. The test has four parts: did the work change what can be credibly known, has it withstood repeated scrutiny and re-analysis, is the credit cleanly attributable, and is the marginal contribution distinct from earlier prizes. I moved from B009 to B030 in round 1 because replication depth and maturity carried most weight for me. Applying that same reasoning to B030 against B005 now points the other way. The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes framework is about three decades old and has been extended, criticised and refined in many applications and by regulators. The colleagues who work closest to the field describe it as a method whose limitations are well known because it has been used so much. B030's core finding of persistent local labour-market costs has held up, but its magnitudes, its persistence and its shift-share identification are still contested, and Strömberg and Fredriksson describe it as only moderately mature. B005 also has the cleanest credit core on the shortlist. Five members independently name the same trio, and Friberg moved to it from Bresnahan. The citation can be limited to demand and competition in differentiated-product markets, so the credit is not diffuse. It also does not sit next to a recent prize in the way B030 (2023, 2024), B014 (2024) and B027 (2022) do, although I have not verified prior-prize scope independently. I do not count the five supporters as merit. Several of them have said that supporter count is not evidence, and I agree. My move rests on maturity, credit clarity and distinctness, which are the criteria I weighted most heavily in round 1. Attribution and validation are the two places where B005 does better than B030 on my own terms.
statement.case_against: My main reservation about B005 is that it is a methods and measurement prize without a single headline finding. Structural demand estimates depend on functional-form, instrument and equilibrium assumptions, and colleagues report that results can be sensitive to implementation. A metascience view is that validation through use is not the same as systematic replication or robustness testing. The record of use is strong, but I cannot independently check how stable individual applications are across specifications, and I did not rank B005 in my opening. My knowledge of the field is thinner than that of Friberg, Andersson or Teorell. The three-name cap also forces a contestable exclusion of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. Compared with B030, B005 says less about distributional consequences and who bears the costs of economic change, a question I care about given the current debates on automation, AI and trade adjustment. B030 has more direct bearing on that question, even though its evidence base is less settled.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson keeps B030 first, treats the China-shock design as a joint Autor-Dorn-Hanson contribution, and prefers Dorn to Katz as third name. She says she would not be unhappy if the committee judged that methodological reach should outweigh substantive findings.
responses.response: We agree on the substance of B030, including the trio and the decision to anchor the citation in the empirical labour-demand evidence rather than the whole task framework. I have not moved because I doubt the design. I moved because, under the same test, B005 is more mature and has a cleaner credit set, while the persistence and shift-share debates you acknowledge are still open for B030. I keep B030 as my first alternative with the same trio and wording. I would also not argue that B005 answers a more important question than who bears the costs of technological and trade change. The two differ on how settled the evidence is, not on how large the question is. I am not suggesting you should move.

responses.point: Friberg revised his third name from Bresnahan to Levinsohn. He argues that diffuse attribution disappears once the citation is limited to demand and competition in differentiated-product markets, and he accepts that implementation sensitivity is a genuine concern.
responses.response: That is the revision that matters most for me, because it makes the credit core uncontested among the supporters. I would keep the citation narrow, as he proposes. If the committee widened it to the new empirical IO tradition, that would be a different prize with a different credit set, and my support should not be read as carrying over to it. I also noted his disclosed field proximity and therefore did not rely on his enthusiasm. I relied on the agreement of colleagues from other fields (Enflo, Strömberg, Teorell and Andersson, who work in other areas) and on the maturity argument. I would ask that the implementation-sensitivity point be stated in the committee's own reasoning, not set aside as evidence of scrutiny alone.

responses.point: Boppart ranked B005 eighth in the opening, was moved by the breadth-of-use argument, and now holds it as his first alternative. He still flags implementation and instrument sensitivity, and he would apply the breadth criterion equally to Kiyotaki-Moore.
responses.response: I agree that the criterion must be applied equally. Under my test, B027 is strongest on originality and credit clarity and weaker on validation, which you and Krusell both say is indirect. B005 is strong on all four parts, with the caveat of implementation sensitivity that you first raised and that I share. The difference between the two caveats is that the B005 limitations have been examined in the open literature, as your own wording suggests, while the amplification mechanism has been validated mostly by others' later work. I do not claim this settles the comparison. Whether a conceptual mechanism outweighs a measurement toolkit with a long record of use is a judgement call that the evidence supplied cannot resolve. I would not call that a weakness in B027, and I would not use it to dismiss Krusell's argument.

responses.point: Hassler, the chair, ranks B014 first and says B005 is close. He would move to B005 if the overlap with the 2024 prize were judged decisive, and he regards B005 as mainly a methods prize that rewards the toolkit rather than a body of substantive findings.
responses.response: My answer to the chair's common-test question is that the committee should ask whether the work changed what can be credibly known and whether that has survived scrutiny. By that test I place B005 first, then B030, and I rate B014 below both because the cross-country identification is weaker, a point you concede. I accept that the Persson-Tabellini formal-model and within-country strands are less exposed. I still cannot tell from the supplied evidence which of B014's results would stand on a design-based standard. I would not make the 2024 overlap a bar, and I do not rely on it. My difference with you is about identification and the strength of the evidence base, not about distinctness. I would also point out that your own conditional move to B005 means the first-choice split overstates the real distance between B005 and B014.

uncertainties: How robust BLP-type estimates are to functional form, instruments and numerical implementation. I rely on colleagues' statements and have not verified this independently, and my assessment is thinner than for B030.
Whether the committee will treat a methods and measurement contribution as equal to a substantive discovery, given that members have not agreed on a single test.

Whether the credit should be limited to Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes with a demand-estimation citation, or widened to the broader empirical IO tradition. That would change the credit set and not only the wording.
How far the persistence, magnitude and shift-share debates should count against B030, and whether Dorn or Katz is the better third name if it is pursued. This affects my first alternative.
Whether the overlap with the 2022, 2023 and 2024 prizes should count as a bar or only as a weight. I have not verified the scope of those prizes independently.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn, or to the credited names on B030 or B009, is apparent from my supplied profile. My listed co-authors and collaborators (Camerer, Pfeiffer, Holzmeister, Huber, Nosek, Rand, Fudenberg, Nowak, Ellingsen, Johannesson and Brodeur) do not appear among the shortlisted credited names. My field is behavioural, experimental and metascience, which is close to B002 but not to my preferred configuration or alternatives. My metascience background leads me to weight replication and design transparency heavily, so I disclose that this lens may favour design-based work and I have tried to apply it to B005 as well. I have co-authored with Ellingsen, a former committee chair, and with Johannesson, a former committee member, but neither is in the current committee or on the shortlist. I note the discrepancy over Teorell and Persson in the chair's summary and do not adjudicate it.
